# THE EAST PLOTS PEN. SEVENTEEN GOATS. NO BODIES. [color=#8A7A62]Pinned. If you keep animals on {colony}, read this one.[/color]
### #1 goat_keeper_ana (OP) // 83.04.20 I keep the goats for the east plots co-op. Milk, mostly, and the kids sell at the founding day market. Seventeen head in the pen as of last night. This morning, none.
The gate was shut and latched. The fence was not broken. On the north side, where the pen backs onto the scrub, there is one gap in the mesh, low down, melted at the edges like the pump house hole in the sightings thread. A gap you could not push a grown goat through. Something did.
There is blood but not much. There are no bodies. Not one. Seventeen animals and not a leg or a horn. There is a drag trail from the gap through the scrub toward the drainage culvert, flattened grass about a metre wide, and on the grass, dried, a brown sticky stuff like tree sap that will not come off your boot.
The goats did not make a sound. My hab is forty metres away. I sleep light. Seventeen goats and none of them screamed.
### #2 tarp_theory // 83.04.20 Rustlers. There are people on this colony who would sell their own grandmother for meat ration credits. Cut the fence with a torch, load them on a hauler, gone by morning.
### #3 goat_keeper_ana (OP) // 83.04.20 Through a hole the size of a ration crate? Towards the drains, not the road? Without one bleat? Go and try to carry a goat that does not want to be carried, then tell me about rustlers.
### #4 vet_tech_on_call // 83.04.21 Clinic, but I do the animals too, because nobody else will. Ana brought me the one thing that was left: a kid, maybe three weeks old, found in the scrub by the drag trail. Dead.
I have looked at a lot of dead animals. This one has one wound. A single round hole in the front of the skull, between where the horn buds would be, about the width of my thumb. It goes straight through to the back. Clean. No tearing around it. Like a bolt gun at a slaughterhouse, except a bolt gun does not go out the other side.
Whatever did this did not bite the animal. It punched it, with something narrow, very fast, from very close. I do not know what has a mouth like that.
### #5 old_rancher // 83.04.22 That is not how a predator kills. A predator wants to eat. This one killed the one it could not carry, and took the rest away alive or near enough. That is not hunting. That is collecting.
### #6 hydro_lettuce // 83.04.23 Can I just say that the brown sticky stuff is on the drainage grate behind hydroponics too. Lots of it. It has set hard like glue and it is warm to the touch. Not sun warm. Warm like skin.
### #7 goat_keeper_ana (OP) // 83.04.26 Update. I reported the pen to colony security. Two officers came, took photos, and told me it was most likely a feral dog and to keep quiet so I did not cause a panic before the harvest festival.
The next day a man from the Company liaison office came on his own. Very polite. Very interested. He took a scraping of the sticky stuff in a sealed jar, and he asked me twice whether anyone had gone into the culvert. He did not ask about the goats at all. He offered the co-op compensation for the herd, more than they were worth, if I signed a form saying they died of a disease.
### #8 tarp_theory // 83.04.27 The Company does not pay over market for diseased goats.
Fine. I am going to go and look in the culvert.
### #9 redwatch_mod (mod) // 83.05.04 Do not go into the culvert.
Ana, if you have not signed the form yet, keep a copy of it unsigned. Keepers of other animals: bring them in at night, all of them, chickens too. Indoors with a door that locks, not just a pen.
